text:
ConocoPhillips rose modestly today, but the stock has fallen nearly 10% over the past two weeks as crude oil prices have slumped. US oil dropped to $99.64 a barrel, and the broader sell-off was triggered by post-election investor concerns about a potential diplomatic breakthrough between the US and Iran — a development that would ease supply-risk premium and increase global oil supply. The company reported quarterly earnings on November 5th, but that announcement coincided with or was overshadowed by the sharp oil price decline.

The tension here is real: energy analysts are warning that renewed US-Iran conflict could push oil back above $100, yet markets are currently pricing in the opposite scenario — a de-escalation and return to lower prices. ConocoPhillips' profit margins compress when crude prices fall, so the stock's weakness reflects investor concern that the oil outlook has softened, at least in the near term.
